searchText: What was the website that tracks The Merge timing? bordel.wtf ? Yeah, thanks. Can we get that pinned <@&595685821026271242>? https://bordel.wtf Current daily hashrate != the polynomial regression of the hashrate used to compute the projection. That makes sense. Nvm When are partial withdrawals enabled? Does that happen immediately post-merge? Bellatrix (the merge fork) does not enable withdrawals. Capella (the fork after Bellatrix) should include withdrawals. Around 1 year to enable then you’ll have to wait your turn which could take months or longer. I thought queue is for exiting as a validator, not withdrawing? I know there will be a queue for withdrawing your staked eth and it’ll be years if everyone does it at once For specifics on a proposed plan that isn’t finalized I can’t help 😅 The exit queue doesn’t apply to partial withdrawals (for earned rewards.) Those will be processed automatically continuously (for a subset of all validators, taking turns) In the event if a black swan type attack on the network, how soon could core devs ship withdrawals? A similar question came up during EIP1559 and the miners show of force, to know when the merge could have been shipped. What is the class of black swan that would require immediate withdraws? It feels like *delaying* withdraws is more likely to be "necessary" (so we can punish people further out). Am definitely against central action taken against individual stakers Power can always be abused and the majority against the minority There is no vote or democratic process. It is just users having the option to have assets on a blockchain that is censored or a blockchain that is not censored. Priority post merge should be on methods to stop censorship of the network and abuse rather than withdrawals 😂 at least that’s my opinion That would be PBS and CR Lists IMO, though not everyone agrees on this. We’re going to see validators block or prefer addresses And no slashing as block is still filled that means basefee just keeps going up before the tx is included I’m personally against slashing as it implies assuming guilt when there could be innocent reasons Unless nearly every validators does it no? Forgive me if I’m mistaken but if validators refuse to pickup a tx in mempool there isn’t a punishment? with crlist they need to fill the block to full or include all tx's from crlist this means that basefee is going up every block before crlist is cleared Interesting I wasn’t aware I guess there is no ready proposals how this would work? there is more research to do but this is a pretty good summary https://notes.ethereum.org/@vbuterin/pbs_censorship_resistance I wrote a reply but deleted it. Sorry. Ethereum is full of different people with different takes on the situation. I was just curious on timelines to get the withdrawal code shipped. I wouldn't think its very complex? the timeline is "Capella" And, yeah, I'm not sure what block swan event specifically hits that intersection of, not catastrophic to PoS as a whole, but warrants an emergency protocol update allowing withdrawals ASAP (because the merge has happened, the chain securing them at that point would be PoS, which ... depends on deposits/stakes). The cause is irrelevant to my question. A black swan event is by definition unknown. My question is only how soon could withdrawals be implemented in an extreme situation? It's ok if the answer is not known. I agree with you in that sentiment Two weeks if your ok with possible bugs and exploits Just like the merge could have happened a year ago Depends on how many corners we want/need to cut. Like any feature, it needs to be designed, then coded (by ~9 different teams), then tested, then released. I can't think of a reason why we would need to rush withdraws compared to say, rushing some upcoming EVM changes though. Feels bizarre to single it out. Especially when the merge was rushed partially due to citing how much is paid versus pos. Financially speaking eth is better off delaying withdrawals so the incentive is to delay it. Withdrawals should be included as fast as possible to reduce market share of staking pools. Recently we've been made aware of how dangerous centralized validator pools might be in terms of censorship. It won't get better as long people cannot withdraw from coinbase&lido to stake at home. There should be public messaging that joining big pools is unhealthy for the network and discouraged. Unless you're taking out TV ads to compete with exchanges, everyone that message would reach already knows that. I don't see how anything changes until withdrawals are enabled. And even then, self-interest is still going to push people to Lido so they can bypass all the barriers you put up.
